## Quarto

```{r load-packages}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r load-relevant-datasets}
#| echo: false
job_posting <- read.csv("https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/Afwans/DATA607-Project3/refs/heads/main/Data/Normalized/JOB_POSTING.csv")

skills <- read.csv("https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/Afwans/DATA607-Project3/refs/heads/main/Data/Normalized/SKILL.csv")

job_posting_cleaned <- read.csv("https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/Afwans/DATA607-Project3/refs/heads/main/Data/job_postings_cleaned.csv")


```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r combining-data}
#Joined the job_posting, the job_skill and the skill data sets
job_skills <- job_posting %>%
  left_join(job_skill, by = "job_id") %>%
  left_join(skills, by = "skill_id") %>%
  select(
    skill_id,
    skill_name,
    job_id,
    title,
    job_category_updated
  )

#Join Check for accuracy
n_distinct(job_skills$job_id)
nrow(job_skills)
n_distinct(job_skills$job_category_updated)

```

```{r summary-table-by-department}

#Removed N/A values
skill_versatility <- job_skills %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(skill_name),
    !is.na(job_category_updated)
  ) %>%
  group_by(skill_name) %>%
  summarise(
    #Counts the number of times a particular skill appears in a job posting
    job_count = n_distinct(job_id),
    
    #Counts the number of times a particular skill appears in a job posting category
    category_count = n_distinct(job_category_updated),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(category_count), desc(job_count))

skill_versatility

```

```{r versatility-heatmap}

#Removes the N/A values
skill_category <- job_skills %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(skill_name),
    !is.na(job_category_updated)
  ) %>%
  group_by(skill_name, job_category_updated) %>%
  summarise(
    job_count = n_distinct(job_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  skill_category,
  aes(
    x = job_category_updated,
    y = skill_name,
    fill = job_count
  )
) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "red"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Versatility of Data Science Skills",
    x = "Job Category",
    y = "Skill",
    fill = "Number of Jobs"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

```

```{r job-versatility-percentages}

#Calculate the total jobs for each category
category_totals <- job_skills %>%
  filter(!is.na(job_category_updated)) %>%
  group_by(job_category_updated) %>%
  summarise(
    total_jobs = n_distinct(job_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#Calculate the total number of jobs requiring that skill of a given category
skill_counts <- job_skills %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(skill_name),
    !is.na(job_category_updated)
  ) %>%
  group_by(job_category_updated, skill_name) %>%
  summarise(
    jobs_requiring_skill = n_distinct(job_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate the percentages job requiring a skill out of the total # of jobs in that category

skill_percentages <- skill_counts %>%
  left_join(
    category_totals,
    by = "job_category_updated"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percentage = round(
      (jobs_requiring_skill / total_jobs) * 100,
      2
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    skill_name,
    desc(percentage)
  )

head(skill_percentages, n=30)

```

```{r heatmap-percentages}
#Creating heat map by percentage covered instead of count
ggplot(
  skill_percentages,
  aes(
    x = job_category_updated,
    y = skill_name,
    fill = percentage
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "darkgreen",
    limits = c(0, 100)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Percentage of Jobs Requiring Each Skill by Category",
    x = "Job Category",
    y = "Skill",
    fill = "Percentage (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

```

```{r ranking-system}

all_skill_percentages <- skill_percentages %>%
  select(
    job_category_updated,
    skill_name,
    percentage
  ) %>%
  #Replaces N/A values with 0.
  complete(
    job_category_updated,
    skill_name,
    fill = list(percentage = 0)
  )

all_skill_percentages

skill_rankings <- all_skill_percentages %>%
  group_by(skill_name) %>%
  summarise(
    
    average_percentage = round(mean(percentage), 2),
    categories_present = sum(percentage > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(average_percentage))

skill_rankings
```
